backtest.grading: spreads and totals at a flat -110 (recorded prices may contain post-tip information, see lines_coverage.json); moneylines at the recorded price (opener price for open_ml). Pushes = 0. Every season is predicted by a model trained on earlier seasons only. Rules are only 'used' (closing / early overall) from the season after they first qualify on earlier seasons (150 bets at the close, 120 at the opener, shrunk ROI > 0, p < 0.10).

record.graded_provider: DraftKings (ESPN provider 100) only; ESPN BET lines archived but not graded (sides cannot be identified)
record.model: learned (LightGBM) minutes x usage x EXPECTED teammate availability x opponent-by-position x market team total, trained only on earlier seasons

model_test.method: Each season projected by a model trained only on earlier seasons; P(over) from a negative binomial whose dispersion was fitted on the previous season's out-of-sample projections. Synthetic lines = the player's last-10-game mean (or median) rounded to the .5 below; baseline P(over) = that stat's over-rate at such lines in EARLIER seasons.

recalibration.method: walk-forward logistic map of the over chance per stat, fitted on earlier seasons' synthetic lines

findings.title: Close to the closing line, not better
findings.text: Over 2,218 out-of-sample games (2018-2026, each season predicted by a model trained on earlier seasons) Locksmith misses the final margin by 9.81 points on average (model alone 9.85); the closing spread misses by 9.60. Totals: 13.43 vs 13.03 for the closing total.

findings.title: Win chances vs the moneyline
findings.text: Log loss of Locksmith's win chance 0.6045 vs the no-vig closing moneyline 0.5876 (lower is better) over 2,207 games.

findings.title: Early-line rules (model vs the opener)
findings.text: Rules chosen each season from earlier seasons only went 367-321 (+5.3% at the opener, 2 of 2 seasons up); the same bets at the closing line: 353-335 (+0.2%). Beat the close 59% of the time.

findings.title: No closing-line rule qualified in the walk-forward test
findings.text: Betting where the model disagrees with the closing spread / total / moneyline never qualified on earlier seasons in any test season: the WNBA closing line already holds what the model knows. On all seasons pooled, close_spread_3.0 now clears the bar, so it is applied live next season, but it has no out-of-sample record yet.

findings.title: Lineups: strictly pre-game (the NBA leak is not repeated)
findings.text: Every projected lineup is rebuilt from earlier box scores only, and recomputing the features with every later box score deleted gives identical values (passed on 12 random dates). When 3+ of the previous game's players sit, a deliberately leaky rebuild (the NBA bug) tracks tonight's actual lineup change at r=0.37; the clean expected lineup at r=0.16.

findings.title: Player projections, tested season by season
findings.text: 41,551 player-games (2018-2026), each season projected by a model trained only on earlier ones, with teammates' availability EXPECTED from earlier games (never from the box score of the night): average miss 4.07 points (last-10 average 4.21), 1.75 rebounds (1.82), 1.20 assists (1.24), 4.7 minutes (5.2). At a line set at each player's last-10 average, Locksmith's over chance scores 0.671 log loss for points vs 0.687 for the base rate.

findings.title: Player props on real sportsbook lines
findings.text: 6,534 real over/under lines (2026-05-08 to 2026-10-26) graded at the OPENING line and price (the latest ESPN prices on finished games are stamped after tip-off, so they are not used): Locksmith log loss 0.6853 vs the book's no-vig opener 0.6887. Rules that made money on earlier days only: 4075 bets, +4.2%. 29 rule(s) qualify now.

findings.title: Price hygiene
findings.text: Spreads and totals are graded at a flat -110 (recorded closing prices can carry in-game information); Action Network consensus rows stamped after tip-off are not used as closing lines; ESPN 'Live Odds' books are dropped; prop prices are graded at the opener only. Moneyline Brier (closing) by season: 2017: 0.176 (expected 0.194), 2018: 0.214 (expected 0.197), 2019: 0.208 (expected 0.204), 2020: 0.185 (expected 0.195), 2021: 0.203 (expected 0.205), 2022: 0.207 (expected 0.206), 2023: 0.194 (expected 0.192), 2024: 0.187 (expected 0.195), 2025: 0.212 (expected 0.192), 2026: 0.199 (expected 0.203).

findings.title: Closing-line edge search
findings.text: Tested 160 rule variants against WNBA closing lines (spreads/totals at -110, moneylines at the recorded price) with walk-forward side/threshold choice and out-of-sample grading (2020-2026). 18 of 56 rules with 150+ OOS bets were profitable out of sample and 0 passed the Benjamini-Hochberg FDR test (q=0.10). The best OOS result was 'early6_fav' (121/205, ROI +12.7%, t=1.93, 5/6 seasons up), not strong enough once ~160 tries are accounted for. No rule survived the full criteria: this search found no reliable edge against WNBA closing lines, and live_candidates() returns nothing. WNBA samples are small (a few hundred bets per rule), so only a large edge could have passed.

findings.title: Who plays matters
findings.text: Every stint since 2015, rebuilt from substitutions, measures each player's impact per 100 possessions (ridge, anchored to her box score, walk-forward). Highest impact going into next season: Veronica Burton, A'ja Wilson, Alyssa Thomas, Angel Reese, Breanna Stewart, Aliyah Boston.

lineups.how_to_read: As-of identity: features recomputed with every box score on/after the cutoff date removed must equal the full-history values (0 difference = the features cannot see tonight). Correlation: the deliberately leaky rebuild (the NBA bug) tracks tonight's actual lineup change far better than any pre-game projection can when players sit; the clean features do not.

props.note: 0 difference = no feature can see the game it projects (teammate availability is EXPECTED availability from earlier games).
